deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 33 is a fair-copy page of notes on ancient political history, continuing from the previous page (Egypt: Necho, Psammis, Apries, Amasis, d. 525). It begins chapter 'VII Karthago'. Content in modern paraphrase:

(1) Heading: 'First period: from the founding of Carthage to the wars with Syracuse, 880–480 [BC]'.

(2) Geography: Carthage lay on a peninsula in the present 'Kingdom of Tunis', joined to the mainland by an isthmus. It had a fortified citadel, Byrsa, and a strong wall across the isthmus.

(3) Founding: 880 BC, by Dido, its founder and first queen.

(4) Early possessions: Sardinia, Corsica, part of Sicily, Majorca, Minorca, Malta, the Canary Islands, etc.

(5) Policy: before the Roman wars the Carthaginians were cautious about conquests on the mainland. They mostly settled on the coasts. Within Africa they expanded as conquerors between about 600 and 500 BC.

(6) The family of Mago founded Carthage's greatness. Mago is said to have been the first to introduce discipline into the army (cf. Justin 18.7: 'primus ordinata disciplina militari').

The periodization (880–480, 480–264) and the topics match A. H. L. Heeren's 'Handbuch der Geschichte der Staaten des Alterthums' (1799 and later editions). This suggests the page is lecture or reading notes on Heeren-style ancient history. The hand and content do not look like Gauss's mathematical work. The bundle label 'HB.Lagrange1816' does not describe this content. Nothing needs reconstructing mathematically.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.
The founding date 880 BC is the older chronology (Heeren et al.). The traditional date is 814/813 BC (Timaeus), so 880 is a period convention, not a slip.
The Canary Islands as an early Carthaginian possession is doubtful by modern standards, but it was a common claim in older handbooks.
The page content does not match the bundle label 'HB.Lagrange1816'. It is likely misfiled, or a non-mathematical notebook (possibly not in Gauss's hand).

results.usually_credited_to: A. H. L. Heeren, Handbuch der Geschichte der Staaten des Alterthums (Göttingen, 1799 ff.); ancient sources Justin, Polybius

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine historical notes on Carthage, closely following standard Göttingen ancient-history teaching (Heeren). It contains no mathematics and nothing original. Its presence in a Gauss bundle is at most an archival curiosity, possibly notes by a family member or student.

checkable.asserts: The first period of Carthaginian history as given spans 400 years.
The second period (stated on the next page, 480–264 BC) spans 216 years.

transcription_corrections: Last line: 'Soll zu erst die Sicilien[?] unter die Römer[?] gebracht haben' should read 'Soll zuerst die Disciplin unter die Armee gebracht haben'. The image shows '...ciplin unter die Armee', which matches Justin's report that Mago first instituted military discipline.

Penultimate passage: 'Größtentheils siedelten sie sich an den Küsten {+und+} innerhalb Afrikas an[?] breiteten[?] sie es als Eroberer...' is better read as 'Größtentheils siedelten sie sich an den Küsten [an]; und innerhalb Afrika erweiterten (breiteten) sie es als Eroberer zwischen 6 und 500 a. C. aus'. '6' here means 600.
Line 2 of body: 'mit dem festen Lande' — 'festen' appears as an interlinear/marked correction in the image.

'Die Größe von Karthago gründete die Familie des Mago' — the image shows 'Mago' at the line end and a struck-through 'Mago' (or 'Mago.') at the start of the next line, consistent with the deletion marked in the transcription.
'Corsika' is written 'Korsika' in the image; 'Kanarische Inseln' is written 'Kanari[sche] Inseln' with an abbreviated suffix.
